full_judgment: 32. Now, if we carefully scrutinise the evidences of these three PWs, it will be found that there are some material discrepancies in their evidences though both of them PWs 2 and 3 are said to be the eye-witnesses of the entire occurrence, but their versions do not appear to be uniform in all material particulars. So far the arrest of this accused is concerned, it is the defence case that this accused was a stamp-vendor and he was returning home from Mohakhali by bus and got down therefrom at the Bangladesh Bank and thereafter he was going towards Tikatuli on foot to catch another bus and on his way near the place of occurrence in a melee he was caught on the road by the public out of suspicion only. In support of his case of defence, this accused appears to have submitted some papers namely, his licence as stamp-vendor and also a paper showing that his father was also a deed writer. There is no denying of the fact that the road wherefrom this accused was caught was a very busy road and it is in evidence that even at about 8-30 PM vehicles were plying on that road. Hence the prosecution case in this back-ground has to be examined in juxtaposition with the defence case. It should be kept in mind that whether the defence succeeds in proving its case or not, the burden of proof on the prosecution to prove its case is never shifted and the prosecution must prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt with reliable and sufficient evidence. In the instant case though there are allegations of demanding subscription from the shop in question and to that effect some evidence is also given, but no specific charge has been made for such allegations under section 2(2) (ক)(অ)of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1992. Now, the only thing which we are to see whether the charge under section 2(2) (ঘ)and (চ)of the said Act has been proved by the prosecution by reliable and sufficient evidence beyound all reasonable doubts, that means whether the accused snatched away any money, ornaments, valuables or vehicles or any other articles by force as defined in section 2(2) (ঘ)of the above Act or collectively or singularly created any disorder or lawlessness by creating terror or fear by force suddenly or by any other means in a house, shop or Bazar or on the road, etc. as defined in section 2(2) (P) of the said Anti-Terrorism Act 1992.
